headline: Prime Value sees News Corp as deeply undervalued with a hidden digital jewel in Dow Jones, worth potentially US$6bn, that is unrecognised in the share price.
reasoning: News Corp owns structurally challenged assets such as newspapers and pay TV that are ascribed a negative value based on the current share price. However, embedded within NWS is a 62% holding in realestate.com.au, one of Australia's best digital businesses, and Dow Jones (including the Wall Street Journal). For the first time NWS disclosed Dow Jones earnings separately, revealing a jewel in the crown — 71% of revenue is digital and earnings increased 13% in the fourth quarter despite COVID disruptions. Peer company The New York Times trades on 25x EBITDA, implying Dow Jones could be worth up to US$6bn, or 70% of NWS's market cap, yet little of this value appears reflected in the share price.
quote: News Corp (NWS) owns a number of old-world structurally challenged assets such as newspapers and pay TV. From a valuation sense these are ascribed a negative value based on the current share price. But also within NWS is a 62% holding in one of Australia's best digital businesses, realstate.com and Dow Jones which includes the Wall Street Journal. For the first time NWS disclosed Dow Jones earnings separately, illustrating a jewel in a crown. 71% of revenue is digital and earnings increased 13% in the fourth quarter despite covid disruptions. Its peer, The New York Times trades on 25x EBITDA, implying Dow Jones could be worth up to US$6bn (70% of NWS), yet there is little ascribed in the share price, in our view.
